title: Index laws: why you add the powers when you multiply
examples: Why do you add powers when multiplying?

items.label: 2⁵ = 32
items.ask: Why do you add powers when multiplying?

explain.say: One cell splits into 2. Then each splits again, and again. Look at the bars: 2, 4, 8, 16, 32. Each one doubles. We write 2 times 2 times 2 as 2 to the power 3. The small 3 is called the index. It counts the 2s.

draw.text: Index laws: why you add the powers when you multiply

items.label: 2⁵ = 32
items.ask: Why do you add powers when multiplying?

explain.say: Look at 2 to the power 3. That is three 2s multiplied: 2 times 2 times 2 is 8. How many 2s are in 2 to the power 2?

items.label: 2⁵ = 32
items.ask: Why do you add powers when multiplying?

explain.say: Two 2s, which makes 4. Now let us multiply them: 2 cubed times 2 squared. That is three 2s, times two more 2s. How many 2s is that in a row?

items.label: 2⁵ = 32
items.ask: Why do you add powers when multiplying?

explain.say: Five 2s! So 2 cubed times 2 squared is 2 to the power 5. Look at the last bar: 32. And 8 times 4 is 32 too. When you multiply, you add the powers: 3 plus 2 is 5.

items.label: 2⁵ = 32
items.ask: Why do you add powers when multiplying?

explain.say: Brilliant! Dividing does the opposite, so you take the powers away. Wow: if you could fold a sheet of paper 42 times, its thickness would double 42 times and, in theory, reach past the Moon! Challenge: write 5 to the 4 times 5 to the 3 as one power.

groups.label: Multiply: add
groups.ask: Why do you add powers when multiplying?

groups.label: Divide: subtract
groups.ask: Why do you subtract powers when dividing?

faq.a: An index, or power, is the small number that says how many times to multiply a number by itself. 2 to the power 3 is 2 times 2 times 2.
asks: What does the small number mean?

faq.q: Why do you add powers when multiplying?
faq.a: Because you are joining strings of the same number. Three 2s times two 2s is five 2s in a row, so 2 cubed times 2 squared is 2 to the 5.

faq.q: Why do you subtract powers when dividing?
faq.a: Dividing cancels matching numbers. 2 to the 5 divided by 2 squared cancels two of the five 2s, leaving 2 cubed.

faq.q: Do the index laws work with different bases?
faq.a: No. 2 cubed times 3 squared cannot be joined into one power, because the numbers being multiplied are different.
asks: Can I add powers of 2 and 3?

faq.q: What is 5 to the 4 times 5 to the 3?
faq.a: Add the powers: 4 plus 3 is 7, so it is 5 to the power 7.

facts: aᵐ × aⁿ = aᵐ⁺ⁿ, aᵐ ÷ aⁿ = aᵐ⁻ⁿ and (aᵐ)ⁿ = aᵐⁿ.
A sheet of paper 0.1 mm thick, doubled 42 times, would be about 440,000 km thick, more than the distance to the Moon.

quiz.say: Simplify x to the 6 times x to the 2.

wrong.1: x to the 12 multiplies the powers, which is the rule for a power of a power.

quiz.say: Simplify 7 to the 9 divided by 7 to the 4.

wrong.1: 7 to the 13 adds the powers instead of subtracting.
wrong.2: The base 7 stays the same; you do not divide it.
